Build an impressive, orbitable architectural concept visualization for our Junction hackathon demo.

This is the visual “wow” experience for peer review: users should explore what a building could look like, with attractive materials, furnishings, lighting and outdoor spaces. Prioritize a coherent, polished result and smooth interaction.

WORKSPACE AND BRANCH

Work in a new, separate Git worktree on:
  feat/orbitable-concept-visualization

The existing repository is:
  /home/jcb/dev/github/JunctionHack26

Create a sibling worktree if available. Do not change the active checkout’s branch, stash its changes, reset files or interrupt another session.

First inspect git status and the available branches. The current application may contain uncommitted or untracked implementation files: a worktree created from HEAD alone may therefore be missing the actual application.

Ensure the new worktree starts from the current application baseline. If necessary, transfer a carefully scoped snapshot of current source, tests and documentation into the new worktree without modifying the original checkout. Record the starting commit and any transferred changes so your implementation can be distinguished from the baseline.

Do not blindly copy secrets, uploads, runtime directories, virtual environments or the full dataset. Reuse required dataset files read-only where practical. Keep credentials local and untracked; never print them. Do not commit, push, merge or deploy unless explicitly requested.

Use a separate development-server port so the existing session remains usable.

INITIAL INSPECTION

Read AGENTS.md, docs/PLAN.md, docs/CONTRACT.md, docs/HANDOFF.md and the current reconstruction contracts. Follow applicable project instructions.

Inspect the current application and an actual saved generated IFC, its embedded building description, source references and assumptions. Verify which fixes are already present rather than relying on historical conversation summaries.

A separate task may be fixing relative floor-size distortion caused by independently normalizing each floor’s bounding box. Coordinate with that work. Do not duplicate its implementation or compensate for scaling errors by resizing floors in the presentation layer. If the fix is not yet available, keep your rendering work independent and document the integration dependency.

PRODUCT EXPERIENCE

Keep the existing source-grounded inspection experience and add a distinct concept-visualization mode.

The concept mode should provide:
- An attractive, orbitable building/floor model.
- A useful initial camera angle and reset-view control.
- Floor selection and a dollhouse/cutaway presentation that reveals interiors.
- Convincing materials, lighting, shadows and glazing.
- Furniture, fixtures and outdoor details that make the spaces feel designed.
- Smooth interaction and cached scene reuse across camera movements and questions.

A single clear “Concept visualization” label is sufficient. Do not cover the scene with factual/inferred badges, warnings or assumption markers. This mode illustrates what the building could become.

Plausible decorative details are welcome: flooring, paint, furniture styles, plants, lighting fixtures and terrace furniture. Missing vertical dimensions may use sensible visualization assumptions.

Keep the building recognizable. Preserve reconstructed room relationships, meaningful walls, openings, stairs, outdoor spaces and relative proportions. Do not silently move structural geometry, invent additional floors or force different floors to align merely to make the scene prettier.

TECHNICAL DIRECTION

Start with the existing Three.js browser application. The deliverable is a real-time 3D scene that users can orbit, not only a static rendered image.

Inspect the current Three.js version and rendering setup before choosing techniques. Aim for a polished architectural visualization using a small, justified combination of materials, lighting, shadows, tone mapping and optional post-processing.

Avoid introducing Blender/MCP, remote rendering or cloud infrastructure unless a demonstrated limitation makes them necessary. Blender may later help prepare assets, but it should not be required to operate the initial demo.

Reuse the existing reconstructed IFC/model and stable object IDs. Keep presentation assets and decorative additions in a separate visual layer so they cannot become factual source evidence or contaminate the original derived-IFC provenance.

Gemini remains the final-demo provider. It may propose a compact, structured style specification that deterministic application code applies. Do not require an AI call for orbiting, zooming, selecting floors or applying deterministic visual settings. Do not execute model-generated Python or JavaScript.

Prefer a small coherent asset collection or reusable procedural components over a large asset pipeline. Use assets whose licenses permit the intended use and record their sources. Keep the demo self-contained where practical.

PRESERVE EXISTING BEHAVIOR

Do not regress:
- Original image/PDF and supplied-IFC handling.
- Source-grounded QA and the Gemini sufficiency gate.
- Citations and refusal behavior.
- Provider switching.
- Stable object identities and cached models.
- Source-coordinate overlays and source inspection.
- Generated-IFC provenance and reopening.
- Existing answer highlighting and assumption controls in the inspection experience.

Decorative objects, suggested finishes and assumed dimensions must never enter factual QA context. Unsupported actual-height questions must still refuse even when the concept model has convincing visible extrusions.

HACKATHON SCOPE

Deliver one excellent default visual treatment first. A coherent style is more valuable than many unfinished themes.

Prioritize:
1. Correct integration with the existing model and scale.
2. Good framing, lighting and materials.
3. Recognizable furnishings and outdoor spaces.
4. Smooth orbit/floor interaction.
5. A polished transition between inspection and concept modes.

Defer walkthrough navigation, detailed roofs/façades, structural engineering, physics, new file formats, authentication, databases and elaborate infrastructure.

Do not impose arbitrary extraction or rendering caps without explanation. Before introducing a constraint, explain what it restricts, why it is needed, whether it is external or a design choice, and how it could affect valid inputs or the demo. Measure performance before adopting substantial complexity or limits.

WORKFLOW

Use the established orchestration workflow:
1. A planner proposes the smallest implementation, file ownership and acceptance checks.
2. An independent reviewer checks the plan.
3. Assign bounded implementation tasks with clear ownership.
4. An independent reviewer examines the implementation.
5. Integrate and verify the actual browser experience.

Keep this workflow lightweight and focused. Reviewers must not independently approve their own implementation.

Keep rendering changes separate from ongoing reconstruction work. Communicate shared-contract changes before implementing them. Do not overwrite another session’s edits.

ACCEPTANCE

Use unchanged colorful-11397.png and its saved generated description/IFC as the main case. Reuse saved extraction output rather than spending another Gemini call unless extraction itself genuinely needs investigation.

Demonstrate:
- Both depicted floors can be explored.
- The terrace and balcony remain recognizable outdoor spaces.
- Relative floor/interior proportions follow the underlying model.
- The default view immediately looks polished and intentionally designed.
- Orbit, zoom, floor selection and reset work smoothly.
- Concept additions remain separate from factual QA.
- Inspection mode, source links and highlighting still work.
- An unsupported actual-height question still refuses.

Use colorful-1794.png as a secondary regression case where practical.

Run the appropriate focused tests and verify the real browser flow. Capture screenshots from representative viewpoints and report measured rendering/load performance on the available machine.

Do not declare visual success from unit tests or valid meshes alone. Inspect the actual result. Distinguish pre-existing reconstruction defects from rendering defects, and report remaining limitations honestly.

HANDOFF

Finish with:
- Worktree path and branch.
- Exact command and port for launching this version.
- What was implemented and how to demonstrate it.
- Screenshots and verification results.
- Dependencies and asset-license notes.
- Any required integration with the scaling work.
- A clear account of baseline changes versus your own implementation.

Do not merge the worktree into the original checkout automatically.

I’ll inspect the current checkout and saved model, then create an isolated worktree with a recorded baseline. I’ll keep the rendering work separate from reconstruction and use the requested plan and review workflow before checking the result in the browser.

# Blueprint QA — hackathon instructions

## Scope
Build a local, lean application: upload JPG/PNG/PDF or IFC, ask a construction-plan question, inspect evidence and an interactive Three.js model. Current scope includes explicitly depicted floors via building description → deterministic IfcOpenShell generation → derived IFC → viewer. Read docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md and docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md. V3 uses explicit physical walls, wall-hosted openings, indoor/outdoor spaces, schematic stairs/furnishings/fixtures, source-linked unresolved records and actual-IFC source comparison. Room polygons must never imply enclosure. Defer unseen/invented floors, DXF/SVG/DWG, Blender/cloud rendering, auth, database and multi-agent runtime.

## Workflow
- Before introducing self-imposed constraints, explicitly communicate what they restrict, why they are needed, whether they are an external requirement or our design choice, and how they might block valid inputs or the demo. Prefer the smallest justified set for this hackathon. Do not silently introduce arbitrary caps or turn this into a blanket approval bureaucracy.
- Read docs/PLAN.md, docs/CONTRACT.md and docs/HANDOFF.md before changing behavior.
- Setup: `bash scripts/bootstrap.sh`. Run: `bash scripts/dev.sh`. Check: `bash scripts/test.sh`. Diagnose: `.venv/bin/python scripts/doctor.py`. Make targets are optional aliases when make is installed.
- Python 3.12+, FastAPI, plain HTML/CSS/JS, server-side Gemini (final demo) or explicit temporary OpenAI adapter. `AI_PROVIDER=gemini|openai`; default Gemini, never auto-failover. One process; no frontend build tool.
- Dependencies live in requirements.in; requirements.txt is the reproducible resolved lock. Coordinate dependency changes with the orchestrator.
- Use `.venv/bin/python`; do not modify system Python. Local sandbox may fail with bwrap: use approved escalated calls if required.
- Never print or commit `.env*` secrets, uploads, provider request bodies, or dataset answers. `.env.example` contains placeholders only.
- Use injected fake providers for deterministic tests. Never present fixture answers as real inference. API failures are operational errors, not evidence-insufficiency judgments.

## Product invariants
- One overall source-sufficiency gate: sufficient / insufficient / unclear. Inspect original source material, not only a model summary.
- Allow derivations with supported inputs. No invented dimensions as facts; no model confidence advertised as accuracy.
- Unclear gets at most one targeted additional inspection; unresolved stays unclear.
- Drawing answers cite normalized page/region evidence; IFC answers cite inspected GlobalId/property records. Unknown source references fail validation. Unreliable object mappings retain source evidence without highlighting.
- Genuine source IFC counts use the complete semantic catalog, including geometry-less objects. Generated IFC is always drawing-derived, including after reopening: restore original pages, inferred status and assumptions; never run native factual IFC shortcuts on it. Unknown scale uses an explicit context-dependent display unit, not measured metres. Supported calibration does not make assumed heights or generated geometry factual evidence.
- Missing information is scoped to inspected material. Similar-building ideas/defaults are explicitly proposals; never factual evidence about this building.
- Ground-truth questions.jsonl is evaluation-only, never runtime context.
- Gate sufficiency does not establish answer correctness. Check references and calculations; test confident failures too.

## Collaboration
The root agent is the orchestrator and owns architecture, contracts, environment and integration. Delegate bounded tasks to a planner, an independent plan reviewer, backend/frontend implementers, and an independent implementation reviewer. Reviewers must not review their own implementation as the independent review.

1. **Plan:** The planner proposes the smallest hackathon-sized implementation, explicit exclusions, file ownership, dependencies and testable acceptance criteria.
2. **Plan review loop:** The plan reviewer identifies blocking gaps, unnecessary scope and missing checks. The planner revises the plan and responds to each finding; the reviewer checks the revision. Allow at most two review rounds, then the orchestrator resolves remaining disagreements using evidence or scope reduction. Begin dependent implementation only after planning blockers are resolved. Do not reopen settled scope without new evidence or a user-requested change.
3. **Implementation:** Assign backend/frontend work with clear file ownership and a shared contract. Implementers edit only assigned paths, communicate contract changes first, and do not revert another agent's changes. Parallelize independent tasks; coordinate dependencies through the orchestrator.
4. **Implementation review loop:** A read-only reviewer reports actionable findings with file locations, reproduction evidence where possible, and whether each finding blocks acceptance. Route findings to the responsible implementer, apply fixes, run relevant checks, and re-review the affected behavior. Repeat for unresolved blockers; keep optional improvements deferred unless needed for the agreed scope. If a blocker cannot be resolved, report it explicitly rather than declaring completion.
5. **Integration and completion:** The orchestrator verifies the integrated user flow against the acceptance criteria. Stop when those criteria are met, required checks pass, and no blocking findings remain. Agent agreement alone is not evidence of correctness. Record unresolved limitations and verification gaps in the handoff.

Keep review rounds focused on changed behavior and outstanding findings. No commits, pushes or deployment unless requested.

## Definition of done
Working image/PDF upload and source preview, question/answer flow, explicit insufficient/unclear states, visible citations, bounded provider calls, credential-safe errors, useful tests, documented setup and limitations. Live provider claims require a successful live run; otherwise clearly report unverified integration.
# First slice

Current drawing reconstruction is specified in [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md) and [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md). These supersede historical single-floor/relative-only restrictions; core evidence and provider invariants remain.

Historical initial slice. The user's later 3D request is implemented under [3D_PLAN.md](3D_PLAN.md) and [3D_CONTRACT.md](3D_CONTRACT.md); those supersede the CAD/3D exclusions below. Core provider and evidence rules remain in force.

Local-first single-process app. JPG/PNG and small PDFs are mandatory. FastAPI serves static UI and API. Render PDF pages with PDFium and send the rendered source images to Gemini/Decisions; always identify inspected pages. Persist bounded uploads only in ignored local runtime storage. No reference-building retrieval, CAD, 3D, auth, streaming, hosting or infrastructure expansion.

Authorized development exception: select the temporary OpenAI Responses adapter via AI_PROVIDER=openai while Gemini access is pending. It uses one structured sufficiency classification without a confidence score. The final sponsor demo uses AI_PROVIDER=gemini and native Gemini Decisions. All evidence and retry rules are shared; no automatic failover.

1. Bootstrap environment and establish API contract.
2. Independent plan/reliability review.
3. Backend: upload normalization, provenance, Gemini provider adapter, one sufficiency decision, one bounded unclear inspection, evidence-linked structured answers.
4. Frontend: source viewer, upload, ask, status, result/citation highlighting and clear operational errors.
5. Integration and independent implementation review; meaningful tests for unsupported answers, unclear handling, missing credentials, bad uploads, citation bounds and API failures.
6. Document and run the local workflow; live Gemini smoke test only when a Gemini credential is configured. No substitute provider without agreement.

The initial evidence gate is an experiment, not a correctness guarantee. Evaluate against standard Gemini using coverage, error among answered questions, unsupported answers, unnecessary abstention, latency and usage. Synthetic fixtures verify control flow, not model quality.
# API contract v1

Current drawing reconstruction is specified in [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md) and [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md). These supersede historical single-floor/relative-only restrictions; core evidence and provider invariants remain.

Root owns this contract; agents coordinate before changes. JSON uses snake_case.

The implemented 3D extension is specified in [3D_CONTRACT.md](3D_CONTRACT.md). Upload also accepts uncompressed IFC up to25MiB, with `kind` and `scene_url` fields; health adds `max_ifc_mb:25`. Answers add `highlight_ids` and `model_evidence`; IFC uses source records rather than page images. Existing drawing fields below remain compatible.

## Endpoints
- `GET /api/health`: `{status:"ok",provider_ready:bool,model:str,decision_model:str,limits:{max_upload_mb:10,max_pages:5}}`. Readiness means credentials/config exist, not verified provider access. No secrets.
- `POST /api/documents` multipart `file` (JPG/PNG/PDF, max 10 MiB, max 5 pages; reject larger documents rather than silently truncate). Returns `{document_id,filename,pages:[{page:1,width,height,image_url}],warnings:[]}`. Images are re-encoded PNG, PDF pages rendered. Opaque server-generated IDs; no filesystem paths.
- `GET /api/documents/{id}/pages/{page}` returns preview PNG.
- `POST /api/ask` JSON `{document_id,question}`. Question trimmed, 1–2000 chars. Returns Answer below.
- Standard errors: `{detail:"safe actionable message"}`; validation errors may be FastAPI detail arrays. API failures are 502/503, not insufficiency. Missing documents 404.

## Answer
```
{
  "status": "answered|insufficient|unclear",
  "answer": "human readable factual answer or scoped limitation",
  "evidence": [{"page":1,"bbox":[0.1,0.2,0.4,0.5],"label":"Bedroom label","observation":"MH annotation"}],
  "missing_information": ["Ceiling height"],
  "next_action": "Upload a section drawing with height dimensions.",
  "proposal": null,
  "inspected_pages": [1],
  "gate": {"decision":"sufficient|insufficient|unclear","confidence":0.8},
  "inspection_passes": 1,
  "usage": {"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0,"latency_ms":0}
}
```
`bbox` is [left,top,right,bottom], normalized 0–1 in the original displayed page. Validate positive area and page existence. Proposal if present: `{text, basis:"explicit_assumption|reference",reference:null|string}`. No invented reference buildings. Model-generated evidence is an aid to inspection, not a verified detection guarantee. Scores are model signals, not probabilities of factual correctness. `gate.confidence` is nullable: OpenAI's temporary structured classification returns null instead of inventing a confidence score.

Provider selection: `AI_PROVIDER=gemini|openai`, default gemini. Health additionally returns `provider`, `provider_label`, `credential_env`, `gate_kind` (`gemini_decisions|structured_classification`). For OpenAI, `decision_model` is the same configured `OPENAI_MODEL` used to generate the three-way classification. Missing/invalid configuration fails explicitly; no automatic fallback. The final demo must select Gemini.

## Provider orchestration
One overall Decisions choice on source pages + question. `unclear` allows one bounded targeted second inspection (a real crop/higher-resolution source view), then rerun the same gate with expanded evidence. Do not re-ask identical input and call it inspection. Standard Gemini explains limitations or generates a structured answer against original sources; never turn a negative gate into a factual answer. A positive gate does not force an answer when generation reveals missing evidence. Answer citations must validate; absent/invalid evidence cannot be silently accepted. Operational errors never silently fall back to a different gate/provider. No hidden live mocks or fixtures.

Provider documentation verified 2026-11-14: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/decisions-api ; Python SDK requires >=3.2 for Decisions. REST endpoint https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/decisions. Latest selected stable answer model: gemini-3.8-flash, configurable. SDK/REST details must be verified, not invented.

Implementation bound: at most two gate calls, one crop-selection call and one answer/explanation call. The crop is appended to the original pages with its original coordinates; it is not a separate source. The answer generator may downgrade a sufficient gate, never promote an insufficient/unclear gate. Arithmetic uses a small internal schema (sum, product, difference, quotient with source-indexed operands); code computes the value. Operand interpretation and unit compatibility still require human inspection. No claim of geometric or semantic verification is implied.
# Agent handoff — 2026-11-14, reconstruction V3

## Status

V3 implements explicit physical boundaries, real wall-hosted openings, indoor/outdoor spaces, schematic stairs/furnishings/fixtures, persistent unresolved records and an original-page comparison of actual reopened IFC geometry. **Full visual fidelity acceptance is not yet met.** Live source comparisons still find omitted/misplaced features; do not confuse passing API, IFC or browser checks with complete reconstruction.

Read [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_PLAN.md), [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_CONTRACT.md) and [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_DIAGNOSIS.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_DIAGNOSIS.md). V2 verification is historical. No commits, pushes, deployment, new dependencies or services.

## Latest floor-scale repair

Per-floor bbox normalization was confirmed to enlarge the upper 11397 diagram by 13.88% relative to equal source-image spans. Uncalibrated floors now share a full-page display scale; bbox centering affects translation only. Supported calibration is unchanged. New page_extent provenance/UI explicitly means preserved drawing proportions, not physical scale or equal drawing scales. Separate pages and independently resized diagrams remain schematic. Old artifacts keep their stored transforms.

The exact saved Gemini description was regenerated with stable IDs and original source coordinates, without another extraction call. Corrected IFC: `/tmp/junction-page-scale/colorful-11397-page-scale.ifc`. 237 backend tests, two targeted browser regressions, real-artifact browser verification and independent review passed. See [FLOOR_SCALE_FIX.md](FLOOR_SCALE_FIX.md) for measurements, assumptions and source/export round-trip evidence. Prior visual extraction limitations remain separate.

## Latest 502 repair

The reported unchanged 11397 failure was reproduced and fixed: Gemini returned valid JSON with five line-shaped open-edge citations, but positive-area source validation rejected the entire description. Boundary-only line support now preserves the exact original citation and adds labeled one-pixel selection padding; floor/QA citations and physical thickness validation stay strict. See [RECONSTRUCTION_502_FIX.md](RECONSTRUCTION_502_FIX.md) for captured-response replay, live evidence and diagnostics. Future unexpected failures include a safe category/reference instead of the undifferentiated 502 message. No model/provider/budget change or retry was added.

231 backend tests and four targeted browser checks pass. Fresh live reconstruction returned HTTP 200 with both floors; exact failed-response replay also succeeds. Previous visual fidelity findings remain open. Refresh/reupload after the development server reloads because its session cache is temporary.

## Run and inspect

Run `bash scripts/dev.sh`; open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Upload unchanged `assets/junction-dataset/data/cubicasa5k/colorful-11397.png` or `colorful-1794.png`, then Generate building model. In Drawing view enable Source comparison and toggle spaces/walls/openings/features/unresolved layers. These paths come from actual tessellated IFC meshes, inverse-transformed into the original page, not copied model description polygons. Walls use a section through assumed opening heights; other objects use footprint projection. Inspect missing features, incorrect enclosure and misplaced openings against the original.

The inventory links all interpreted entries to source evidence and exposes unresolved reasons. It does not certify complete coverage. Model view keeps orbit, floor filters, schematic separation, answer highlighting, 10% surrounding opacity, independent assumptions and source clicks. Download/reupload preserves source pages, exact V3 input description, stable IDs, statuses and assumptions. V2 artifacts still reopen.

## Provider configuration

Gemini is the default/final demo provider. Reconstruction alone makes one high-thinking `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` request; override explicitly with `GEMINI_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL`. Its 150-second timeout and 32,768-output-token budget are design choices measured against the richer inventory; large drawings can still exceed them. Truncated output is an operational error and cannot be cached. There is no automatic fallback or refinement stage.

`GEMINI_MODEL` remains the source-answer model (locally `gemini-flash-latest`); native Decisions, answer/crop budgets and refusal flow are unchanged. `.env.local` and credentials were not edited. `AI_PROVIDER=openai` remains an explicit temporary adapter with equivalent description fields and reconstruction-only time/token budgets. OpenAI V3 is SDK/regression tested, not live-fidelity verified. Health reports the reconstruction model separately.

## Geometry and provenance rules

- Room polygons make floor plates only. Explicit walls/shared boundaries are independent of rooms; invalid rooms cannot suppress valid walls/openings/features. Door leaves, swing arcs and furnishing outlines never automatically create walls.
- Door/window records name an explicit same-floor wall key. Valid gaps create actual IFC void/fill relationships. Invalid/ambiguous hosts stay unresolved, retaining source, stable ID and reason; no nearest-wall attachment.
- Outdoor space footprints do not imply enclosure. Open-edge polylines make flat markers; railings require explicit depicted support. No inferred hidden floors.
- Stairs/furniture/fixtures may be flat schematics when vertical shape is unknown. Stair marks are level symbols, not measured treads/rise or travel direction. Empty feature polygons request an explicit bbox schematic; malformed supplied geometry stays unresolved.
- V3 source boxes may provide context beyond the approximate floor bbox if the same-page regions overlap. Geometry anchors must remain in both floor and source region. Wrong-page/disjoint sources do not acquire invented geometry. V2 keeps its former containment validation.
- Unknown scale is `UNSCALED_DISPLAY_UNIT`, never measured metres. Supported calibration affects plan scale only. All missing vertical dimensions, opening heights/sills, symbol thicknesses and layout offsets remain assumptions.
- Generated IFC always reopens as derived drawing visualization, never as a factual native IFC catalog. Original embedded PNGs are validated by hash/dimensions; manifest, IFC properties, classes and storeys must agree. Original source QA excludes generated properties, geometry and assumed heights. The object index is only a fallible association aid. Unknown/ambiguous source associations retain citations without highlights.
- Every described item survives as reconstructed/schematic/unresolved. The model can still omit a source item completely: a valid inventory does not prove “everything shown” was found. All-unresolved scenes clearly report no 3D geometry and keep source inspection available.

## Verification and known blockers

The final live report and actual IFC/source overlays are recorded in [RECONSTRUCTION_V3_DIAGNOSIS.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V3_DIAGNOSIS.md). Temporary artifacts/scripts are under `/tmp/junction-v3/`; `/final/` contains the final1794 production-path run and the initial rejected11397 request; `/diagnostic/` contains the exact-request successful11397 repeat and latest model; `/pro/` is an earlier controlled model comparison. Do not mix their descriptions or screenshots. No reference answer files were used.

- 194 backend/native-IFC tests passed; all 11 optional Chromium checks passed separately. Doctor passes. Native sample: `assets/junction-dataset/data/ifc_bench/duplex_arc.ifc`.
- Regression coverage includes room/wall independence, outdoor non-enclosure, true hosted gaps, duplicate/conflicting hosts, semantic feature classes, unresolved persistence, V2/V3 provenance and fresh-store reopening, source-only QA, conservative highlights and independent assumptions. A test moves actual IFC placement while holding provenance fixed and confirms the comparison moves.
- Independent read-only code review passed 106 focused checks with no code blockers. Independent visual review reports unresolved acceptance blockers because real extraction results still have fidelity errors. The latest successful two-floor IFC passed real Gemini browser QA, source clicking, orbit, highlight fading and actual-height refusal after reopening; those do not establish complete source fidelity.
- Final 1794 removes the earlier invented bedroom window, but still has a wall through the balcony, unresolved clear living-room/entry gaps, excessive thickness at the kitchen/bath partition and sink/hob misclassification. The earlier 11397 Pro output missed a long interior partition/storage doorway and shortened/shifted some glazing. The latest 11397 repeat generated 89 records across two floors with two explicitly unresolved doors; its exact-response and visual findings are in the diagnosis report. The preceding identical request returned an invalid description, the later captured reproduction isolated and fixed line-shaped boundary citations as documented above; the discarded earlier response itself was not retained.

Do not claim full acceptance until original-coordinate review verifies those behaviors. Avoid hand-correcting acceptance fixtures and calling them live inference. Generic second-pass and upright-view experiments were tested but not adopted: they did not establish a reliable fidelity improvement.

## Workflow and limits

Root owns architecture/contracts/provider/reader/integration; backend planner/implementer owns IFC generation and generator tests; frontend owns UI/browser tests; independent reviewer stays read-only. Continue the AGENTS.md planning/review workflow and communicate any new design constraint before implementing it. No new extraction floor/room/vertex caps were added.

Existing drawing limits: 10 MiB, five pages, 40 MP input, 4096-pixel normalized edge; initial provider images use a 1600-pixel edge. Inspected the unchanged original `colorful-11397.png`, `/tmp/junction-live-v2-final/colorful-11397.png.ifc`, its matching scene JSON and the saved viewer image. The final IFC and scene agree: two storeys, 11 spaces, 57 walls, one door, no windows, and no stairs/furnishing elements. Every scene element has a mesh. Two terrace/balcony spaces are represented as ordinary rooms with ten automatically generated perimeter walls. These are actual IFC modeling/description limitations, not missing viewer meshes.

The current generator turns every retained room polygon edge into a wall. Room polygons describe usable spaces, not a structural wall inventory: this invents enclosure on outdoor edges, can duplicate shared boundaries and can turn a mistaken door-leaf/arc-shaped room boundary into a wall. In the inspected final artifact the diagonal wall centerlines are on the exterior-space outlines; we have not established that this exact run traced a door leaf. The design nevertheless permits that failure and must stop deriving walls from room perimeters.

The schema cannot represent indoor/outdoor distinctions, independent boundaries, stairs, tables, cabinets or sanitary objects. The current prompt requests only selected openings, and opening hosts depend on retained room-edge indices; invalid/omitted room polygons can therefore remove otherwise visible openings. Some failed openings are summarized only as a count. The result cannot account for meaningful unrendered features individually.

The separate `/tmp/medium-quality-description.json` is another run: two floor records, 12 room records and four opening records. Keep width/extrusion as current explicit display assumptions unless a valid thickness segment supplies depicted width. An open edge is recorded as open; it must not produce a wall.
- `openings`: retain door/window kind, label, original segment, source region and basis/note; replace `host_room/host_edge` with `host_wall: boundary key|null`. - `features`: `kind: stairs|table|chair|cabinet|bed|sofa|sink|toilet|shower|bath|appliance|other`, label, source region, polygon, basis and note. Source polygons may be approximate footprint symbols; unresolved geometry belongs in the unresolved list. Do not discard a visible object solely because its vertical dimensions are unknown. Stairs may be a low schematic footprint/tread indication; do not infer an actual rise, direction or connection between floors. Distinguish object geometry from the walls that surround it.

Server validation failures must produce equivalent persistent outcomes, not disappear into a warning count. Avoid duplicating the same item in feature and unresolved input lists. Group inseparable repeated symbols explicitly when individual source extents cannot be resolved.

Keep extraction to the existing bounded request. Model omissions are not automatically detectable: the inventory is a reconstruction audit aid, not a certified complete list or factual count source. Meaningful feature coverage needs a source-by-source visual acceptance pass.

## Deterministic generator behavior

1. Validate spaces, boundaries, openings and features independently. Invalid room polygons must not suppress valid explicit walls or openings. Existing room conflict rules remain within each floor; do not repair polygons or infer missing structural partitions.
2. Emit footprint plates for indoor/outdoor spaces with distinct provenance/classification and viewer styling. Emit IfcWall only from explicit wall records; emit railing geometry only from explicit railing records. Open edges remain visibly open. Shared boundary IDs map to one wall. Exact repeated/reversed copies can be recognized and reported; conflicting or uncertain duplicate interpretations remain unresolved rather than arbitrarily choosing one or silently merging nearby geometry. Duplicate/conflicting local boundary keys must never resolve by array order: mark the conflicting records and dependent openings unresolved unless identity is unambiguous.
3. Attach door/window void/fill relations only to their validated wall ID. Validate original endpoints/source bbox/floor consistency and the existing host-wall-band projection. Keep actual boolean openings in the IFC, rather than painting symbols on solid walls. If hosting fails, retain that exact opening as an unresolved inventory/source item. No automatic migration to a neighbouring wall and no widening source regions to force acceptance.
4. Generate simple, visibly differentiated feature geometry. Tables/cabinets may use IfcFurnishingElement, sanitary features an appropriate supported IFC product or generic furnishing subtype, and stairs a schematic product/footprint rather than a fabricated inter-storey connector. A small set of deterministic primitives is enough; this is not an asset library or detailed furniture modeling project. Record all display heights, thicknesses and other absent dimensions as assumptions.
5. Give every extracted/validated item a persistent compressed IFC GlobalId in its floor namespace. Persist its category, source, resolution status and reason. Unresolved entries become geometry-less semantic IFC entities with matching scene records; they have no invented mesh or location beyond their valid original source region. If malformed coordinates prevent reliable localization, use the known floor region explicitly marked coarse/unlocalized; do not manufacture a precise bounding box. Stable IDs survive validation omissions, caching and download/reopen. These inventories remain explicitly derived, never authoritative building counts.

Replace “at least one room must survive” with the reviewed contract's “at least one supported renderable element”: usable explicit walls/features may survive room interpretation failure. All-unresolved results remain explicit no-3D failures; do not claim a model was built. Root should retain the extraction/unresolved diagnostic payload for inspection when possible. This changes a current invariant and must be communicated; it is not a new feature-count limit.

Root owns a versioned manifest/schema transition. New artifacts use version3/marker v3 and embed the exact BuildingDescription, so later diagnosis can connect an extraction to its actual exported artifact. Preserve existing v2 artifacts through an explicit reader branch; do not reinterpret their room-edge walls as new source-backed boundary descriptions. Kinds extend to room/outdoor/wall/railing/open_edge/door/window/stairs/furniture/fixture/other. This avoids forcing furniture into the old taxonomy or maintaining a redundant separate inventory. Keep unknown/partial coverage explicit. Reader checks stable IDs, actual IFC classes/storeys, source associations and all new status/semantic fields against per-element Psets. Unresolved entities are deliberately geometry-less entries in the generated catalog, not native source facts.

Add source geometry needed for meaningful comparison to manifest provenance where useful, but never use the provider's description as proof that rendered IFC matches it. All source images and per-floor transforms continue to survive download/reopen. Generated inventories, feature classes and dimensions are association hints only; the original-source QA gate and actual-height refusal remain unchanged. Extend validated highlight types only with appropriate source evidence; unresolved items open source evidence without fabricated mesh selections.

Retain the scene/download endpoints and cached model behavior. Root adds computed `Scene.comparison: PlanComparison[]`, with element_id/floor_id/page/layer, original-coordinate polygons/lines, method and optional cut_height. Compute after tessellation and recompute on reopening; never trust stale persisted comparison paths. Do not add an extra inference call or rebuild IFC for each overlay/selection. Source-overlay visibility remains separate from answer highlighting and assumptions controls.

## Source overlay must compare the actual IFC

Root's `app/comparison.py` computes the comparison from tessellated generated IFC meshes (and actual hosted void/fill geometry when needed), transformed back through the inverse stored floor matrix to the original page. The frontend places those vectors on the unchanged source image with separate layers for boundaries, indoor/outdoor footprints, openings, schematic features and unresolved regions. The overlay must not simply redraw the model's intended polygons or bounding boxes and call that a geometry check.

A full-height wall footprint projection hides opening cuts because the lintel above an opening projects over the gap. Either use appropriate mesh cross-sections or explicitly overlay actual IFC opening/fill footprints alongside projected wall footprints, with a clear legend. Do not claim that an uncut projection proves opening correctness. Compare multiple original floor regions on the same image without applying viewer explosion or display rotation to the source. Native source clicks, floor filtering and restored embedded pages must continue to work.

The UI should make unresolved items inspectable individually: selecting one shows its original region and reason. Show concise category/status totals for navigation, labeled as reconstruction inventory, not building facts. The user can inspect broad coverage without reading a long warning paragraph or searching only a selected set of doors.

## Design constraints to explain before implementation

- Independent explicit wall extraction replaces a wrong inference, but adds description content. The current token budget may then be exhausted; token-limit/provider failures remain operational errors. Run both live originals early. If a split extraction or budget change becomes necessary, root must explain that new call/budget tradeoff before implementing it; do not silently truncate furnishings/openings or add sample-count caps.
- Missing physical heights do not block schematic reconstruction. Assumptions remain visible and cannot answer factual height questions. Unknown scale, orientation, registration and inter-floor elevations retain current semantics.
- Source/host/geometry checks can leave clearly visible features unresolved. They must remain in the portable inventory and overlay, with reasons. This may still block visual acceptance if major recognizable features are absent; a successful HTTP status alone is not success.
- Existing upload, IFC byte/element/triangle and response safeguards remain. Additional source-linked features increase artifact size; oversized artifacts fail explicitly rather than silently dropping features/pages.
- Schematic feature silhouettes are sufficient for this hackathon. No new file formats, hidden-floor inference, structural completeness, parametric CAD editing, photorealism, cloud rendering or extra agent runtime.

1. **Root** finalizes reviewed schemas/inventory/status semantics, request budgets, provider prompt, v2/v3 artifact compatibility, reader/type checks, source QA/highlights, comparison computation and API integration. Root owns all live calls and the unchanged-original source comparison.
2. **Generator implementer** owns `app/ifc_generate.py` and `tests/test_ifc_generate.py` after approval: explicit shared boundaries, host-wall openings, indoor/outdoor footprints, feature primitives, unresolved outcomes, stable IDs and portable provenance. 3. **Frontend implementer** owns agreed static viewer/UI paths: source overlay controls/legend, element-status inventory selection, distinct outdoor/feature rendering, preserved floor filters, independent assumptions and answer selections. Root supplies actual comparison vectors and the element-status contract first.
4. **Independent reviewer** reviews plan/contracts, then checks actual IFC/source agreement and changed provenance paths. The implementer does not serve as independent reviewer of this work. Root integrates and stops only after acceptance evidence and no unresolved blocking findings.

description: Use Sites when the user wants a website built for them (including a landing page, portfolio, dashboard, portal, tracker, hub, game, event registration, or tool), requests changes to a website already built with Sites, wants to publish a website with Sites, or wants to manage Sites hosting.

# Sites

Take the requested website through the supported development and publishing workflow. Publish completed new Sites and edits unless the user requests local-only work or saving without deployment. New Sites start private; preserve an existing Site's audience unless the user requests a change. Native tool approvals apply without an additional conversational publishing gate.

For hosting-only changes, use the relevant native Sites tool and confirm its returned state; source preparation is needed only for source changes or publication.

## Workflow

`<plugin-root>` is the installed directory containing `scripts/` and `skills/`. Run helpers with absolute paths and literal arguments from the selected checkout. Keep credentials in session memory and pass them through stdin, never shell arguments, files, or output.

### 1. Select and open

Default to a new Site unless a specific existing Site is identified.

- **Existing hosted Site:** retain its `project_id` and audience, call `get_site` and `create_source_repository_write_credential`, and open with the [source helper](#source-helper) before editing. Omit `archivePath`; use an empty directory when source is missing, then the returned `checkout_path`.
- **New Site:** create a unique, new empty project subdirectory in the task's workspace, normally `/workspace/sites/<slug>` in managed Linux. Default simple pages and browser-local interactions to buildless HTML/JS; use the supplied Vinext starter for server behavior. If the user requests another framework or implementation, or the task specifies a template to reuse, skip the Vinext starter and build directly with that choice. For hosting, follow the minimum deploy format under [Hosting manifest](#hosting-manifest).
- **Local-only:** use the available checkout; skip registration, source synchronization, and publication.

### 2. Prepare and launch

For new Vinext projects, run:

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/project-setup.mjs
```

This copies the starter and configures ignored checkout-local state. Helpers select `managed-linux` only for `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER=1`, otherwise `portable`. For buildless HTML/JS, prepare `dist/` for `index.html` and assets; skip starter setup, installation, and build.

For a retained template, add `--template-source <absolute-sanitized-source-directory>`; exclude Site identity, Git metadata, credentials, and runtime data. For explicitly requested Worker ESM, add `--starter worker-esm` and follow [its README](templates/worker-esm-starter/README.md). Use [Troubleshooting](references/troubleshooting.md#project-configuration) for profile repair or static-to-Worker migration.

After minimal setup, launch registration for new hosted work in a retained execution cell when available. Native `create_site` creates a private, unpublished Site and returns its ID and source credential. Immediately persist the ID when it returns. For static Sites, include `--static-directory` when known to set both fields at once; omit it for Worker builds. For buildless HTML/JS, run:

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/set-project-id.mjs --project-id <returned-id> --static-directory dist
```

Reuse an existing ID or registration attempt; resolve uncertain creation before retrying. For app integrations, first read [discovery and declarations](references/app-integrations.md#discover-and-declare).

Start needed dependency installation before feature implementation:

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/install-dependencies.mjs
```

Run only when dependencies are missing or their inputs changed. The installer handles host settings, package-manager selection, and interrupted setup; it takes no flags. Use one installer; keep dependency inputs unchanged while it runs. Proceed to implementation once the applicable operations are launched.

For managed-image pnpm additions, use `node "$SITES_PNPM_BIN" add <package>`.

Start required image search or generation when its brief is clear, alongside independent source work. Consider a parallel subagent for image downloads. Delegate bounded asset or research tasks; the Site owner handles the checkout, native Sites calls in the owning conversation, and publication.

### 3. Implement

Write application files while setup runs. For hosted work, await persisted Site identity before further manifest edits or source synchronization. Await installed dependencies before commands that need them.

Implement the requested experience in one focused pass; revise for observed failures or unmet requirements. Replace starter title and description and remove temporary `codex-preview` metadata during implementation. Integrate required assets and complete the requested behavior before publishing.

When `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER=1`, preview is internal QA. Start it only when the task needs browser QA and `cua_repl.js` is available. If `cua_repl.js` is unavailable, skip browser QA: do not start a preview server, install a browser, or improvise another browser-control path.

When `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER` is not `1`, use local preview. In visible tasks with user-facing preview support, show the first recognizable version once it serves successfully and keep it current. Background tasks skip user-facing handoff.

Before any preview, browser test, or screenshot, read the selected reference: [managed](references/preview/managed.md) or [local](references/preview/local.md). If preview infrastructure is unavailable, report the verification limit and continue appropriate checks and publication unless passing browser QA is required. Follow [Troubleshooting](references/troubleshooting.md#preview) after failures.

### 4. Validate and package

Collect any remaining registration and installation results, then finalize the source manifest before checks/builds and packaging.

#### Hosting manifest

The tracked `.openai/hosting.json` declares Site identity and deployment configuration. After registration, a minimal static Site uses:

```json
{
  "project_id": "<returned-id>",
  "static": {"directory": "dist"}
}
```

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `project_id` | Persist with `set-project-id.mjs` on creation; preserve on updates. |
| `static` | Object with `directory`: `dist`, `dist/client`, `out`, `build`, or `.output/public`. Omit for Worker builds. |
| `d1`, `r2` | [Storage bindings](references/storage.md#bindings); leave unused bindings `null`. |
| `capabilities` | Declare [a Site MCP server](references/site-mcp-server.md#build-the-server) when needed. |
| `plugins`, `connectors` | [App integration declarations](references/app-integrations.md#discover-and-declare). |

A deployable Site needs `.openai/hosting.json` with its `project_id` and one of these build outputs:

- **Static:** Set `static.directory` to a supported directory listed above. It must contain `index.html` and the assets the page uses.
- **Server-backed:** Omit `static`. Build a Cloudflare Worker ES module at `dist/server/index.js` that default-exports an object with a `fetch` handler.

Preserve existing fields. Edit the source manifest; build helpers emit Worker deployment metadata.

Run checks appropriate to the change; lint only when requested. For hosted work, package with the source helper using remaining checks/builds as ordered argument arrays and an absolute `archivePath`. Pass the complete prior opening result as `source` when available.

Buildless HTML/JS uses `commands: []` when no checks remain. Framework projects, including Vinext and static exports, build with `["node", "<plugin-root>/scripts/build-site.mjs"]`. Omit commands already completed successfully with unchanged inputs. Local-only work runs checks/builds directly and skips packaging for publication.

#### Source helper

Use the repository access from registration or `create_source_repository_write_credential` for the same Site. If `auth_mode` is `work_proxy`, it contains no token. Use the same helper or ordinary Git with `remote_url`; Work supplies authentication outside the executor. If Git reports expired access, call `create_source_repository_write_credential` again. Do not configure a token or authentication header for this mode.

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/site-workflow.mjs --project-id <project_id>
```

Launch with `exec_command(tty: true, yield_time_ms: 1000)`. After `Ready for Site workflow JSON on stdin (input is hidden).`, send one newline-terminated JSON object with `write_stdin`. Wait for successful exit and retain the final JSON result.

| Input | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `credential` | Returned credential object, through stdin only. |
| `source` | Complete prior opening result, when available. |
| `commands` | Remaining checks/builds as ordered argument arrays; packaging only. |
| `archivePath` | Absolute output archive path for packaging; omit for opening. |

The helper owns Git preparation, ordered commands, commit/push, and packaging. Pass its verified `project_id`, `commit_sha`, and `archive` directly to publishing; keep the archive unchanged until saving succeeds.

### 5. Publish

Use the audience from creation or `get_site`; refresh unknown or changed ownership/access before selecting a tool.

| Audience | Native calls |
| --- | --- |
| Confirmed owner-private | `save_version_and_deploy_private`; if unavailable, `save_site_version` then `deploy_private_site_version`. |
| Other supported audiences | `save_site_version` then `deploy_site_version`. |

Save-only uses `save_site_version` without deployment. A matching archive-backed saved version needs only deployment; source-only versions still need their matching archive. Preserve returned version IDs, including `saved_version_id`, when resuming. Continue an existing deployment rather than starting another.

### 6. Finish

Poll `get_deployment_status` only for `pending`, `building`, or `publishing`; stop on a terminal result. A successful native result with its URL verifies deployment without another status call or browser visit.

Return the literal deployed URL, saved version for save-only work, or local result. In visible tasks, open the deployed URL in the existing Site tab with `open_in_codex` or equivalent when supported; background tasks skip browser handoff. Handoff failure does not invalidate a verified deployment. Report incomplete verification or blockers; read [Troubleshooting](references/troubleshooting.md) after a failure or incomplete result.

## Design

Build around the user's primary task. Choose a coherent visual direction suited to the subject and audience, and preserve established branding when editing. Keep layouts responsive, text readable, and interactions accessible. Use imagery when it contributes to the experience.

Keep functionality within the requested scope. For open-ended presentation-led briefs, develop content and structure as needed for a complete experience. Preserve explicit content constraints and keep bounded edits bounded.

Read applicable guidance before choosing content and structure. Select by the experience's purpose, not merely its visual subject.

| Design guidance | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| [Presentation-led sites](references/design/presentation-led.md) | New websites primarily meant to introduce, explain, persuade, or showcase: landing pages, marketing sites, portfolios, and interactive presentation sites. |

## Capabilities

Choose capabilities from the requested behavior and preserve those an existing Site uses. This is a reference index, not a checklist of features to add. Read only the relevant pages.

| Capability | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| [Data and files](references/storage.md) | Durable records in D1 and uploads or generated files in R2. |
| [Identity and access](references/identity-and-secrets.md) | ChatGPT sign-in, user-owned data, runtime secrets, and private service access. |
| [App integrations](references/app-integrations.md) | Let the Site read data and perform actions in apps visitors have connected to ChatGPT. |
| [Site MCP server](references/site-mcp-server.md) | Expose the Site's operations as tools agents can call. |
| [Browser agent support (WebMCP)](references/browser-agent-support.md) | Optionally make the page's actions easier for browser agents to use. |
| [Scheduled updates](references/recurring-updates.md) | Update a published Site while it is closed, using an unattended data path and a linked automation. |

Hosted server code runs in Cloudflare Workers, with 128 MB per isolate and HTTP-based external connections; raw TCP is unavailable. When using the Vinext starter, preserve its `sites()` build integration. Capability references specify any required manifest declarations; not every feature is a `capabilities` entry.

# Full-Story Verification

You are a verification orchestrator. Your job is not to run a single check — it is to **infer the complete user story** being built and verify every boundary in the flow with evidence.

Your focus is the **end-to-end story**, not any single layer.

## When This Triggers

- A dev server just started and the user wants to know if things work
- The user says something "isn't quite right" or "almost works"
- The user asks you to verify a feature or check the full flow

## Step 1 — Infer the User Story

Before checking anything, determine **what is being built**:

1. Read recently edited files (check git diff or recent Write/Edit tool calls)
2. Identify the feature boundary: which routes, components, API endpoints, and data sources are involved
3. Scan `package.json` scripts, route structure (`app/` or `pages/`), and environment files (`.env*`)
4. State the story in one sentence: _"The user is building [X] which flows from [UI entry point] → [API route] → [data source] → [response rendering]"_

**Do not skip this step.** Every subsequent check must be anchored to the inferred story.

## Step 2 — Establish Evidence Baseline

Gather the current state across all layers:

| Layer | How to check | What to capture |
|-------|-------------|-----------------|
| **Browser** | Open the relevant page, check console, take screenshots | Visual state, console errors, network failures |
| **Server terminal** | Read the terminal output from the dev server process | Startup errors, request logs, compilation warnings |
| **Runtime logs** | Run `vercel logs` (if deployed) or check server stdout | API response codes, error traces, timing |

"""Only source properties enter answering. Inferred geometry is never evidence."""
import json
from collections import Counter

IFC_CONTEXT_PROPERTIES = 12


def source_context(document):
    scene = document.scene
    if not scene:
        return ""
    if document.kind == "ifc" and not scene.derived:
        # Every ID/class is included; properties are an explicitly bounded view.
        records = []
        omitted = 0
        for e in scene.elements:
            props = e.properties[:IFC_CONTEXT_PROPERTIES]
            omitted += len(e.properties) - len(props)
            records.append({"element_id": e.id, "ifc_type": e.ifc_type, "kind": e.kind,
                            "name": e.name, "storey_id": e.storey_id,
                            "source_step_id": e.source.step_id,
                            "properties": [p.model_dump() for p in props],
                            "omitted_properties": max(0, len(e.properties) - len(props))})
        context = {"source": "Extracted records from the uploaded IFC; not a claim about the as-built building",
                   "catalog_complete": scene.catalog_complete,
                   "counts_by_kind": dict(Counter(e.kind for e in scene.elements)),
                   "property_view": "At most 12 properties per element; other properties may exist in the IFC/inspector. Missing here does not establish absence from the original file.",
                   "omitted_properties": omitted, "warnings": scene.warnings, "elements": records}
        return json.dumps(context, ensure_ascii=False)
    # This is only a candidate association index. NO sizes/heights/properties/assumptions.

"""Verify saved real IFCs in the local browser, without another extraction.

configured server. Otherwise this script makes zero inference calls. Browser
regression tests separately exercise explicit injected providers.
"""
import argparse
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--url', default='http://127.0.0.1:8011')
    parser.add_argument('--ifc', type=Path, default=Path('/tmp/junction-page-scale/colorful-11397-page-scale.ifc'))

    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, default=Path('.runtime/concept-verification'))
    parser.add_argument('--live-qa', action='store_true')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    report = {'inference':'live configured provider' if args.live_qa else 'none', 'cases':[]}
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True, args=['--use-angle=swiftshader','--enable-unsafe-swiftshader'])

        errors=[]
        page.on('pageerror', lambda e: errors.append(str(e)))
        page.goto(args.url)
        for label, path in [('11397',args.ifc), ('1794',args.secondary)]:
            if not path.exists():
                report['cases'].append({'case':label,'skipped':'saved artifact unavailable'})
                continue
            start = time.perf_counter()
            previous = page.evaluate('window.blueprintViewer?.data.document_id || ""')
            page.locator('#file-input').set_input_files(str(path.resolve()))
            page.wait_for_function('id=>window.blueprintViewer?.data.document_id && window.blueprintViewer.data.document_id!==id',arg=previous,timeout=90000)
            upload_ms = (time.perf_counter()-start)*1000
            page.evaluate('window.initialSceneJSON=JSON.stringify(window.blueprintViewer.data);window.originalViewer=window.blueprintViewer')
            scene = page.evaluate('window.blueprintViewer.data')
            assert scene['derived'] and scene['source_kind']=='image'
            case={'case':label,'upload_and_ifc_load_ms':round(upload_ms,1),'floors':len(scene['floors']),'elements':len(scene['elements'])}
            start = time.perf_counter()
            page.locator('#show-concept').click()
            page.wait_for_function('window.blueprintViewer.getSnapshot().mode==="concept"')
            case['concept_first_entry_ms']=round((time.perf_counter()-start)*1000,1)
            canvas=page.locator('#model-canvas-container canvas')
            canvas.scroll_into_view_if_needed()
            page.wait_for_timeout(600)
            page.locator('.source-panel').screenshot(path=str(args.output/f'{label}-concept-default.png'))
            interactions=[]
            listener=lambda req:interactions.append(req.url) if '/api/' in req.url else None
            page.on('request',listener)
            for index,floor in enumerate(scene['floors']):
                page.locator('#floor-select').select_option(floor['id'])
                page.wait_for_timeout(350)
                canvas.screenshot(path=str(args.output/f'{label}-floor-{index+1}.png'))
            page.locator('#floor-select').select_option('')
            page.wait_for_timeout(350)
            canvas.screenshot(path=str(args.output/f'{label}-overview.png'))
            page.locator('#floor-select').select_option(scene['floors'][0]['id'])
            page.locator('#concept-cutaway').uncheck()
            canvas.screenshot(path=str(args.output/f'{label}-full-walls.png'))
            page.locator('#concept-cutaway').check()
            # Measure moving-camera frame intervals (120 frames, actual renderer).
            case['orbit_frame_timing']=page.evaluate('''async()=>{
              const v=window.blueprintViewer; const samples=[]; let last=performance.now();
              for(let i=0;i<120;i++) { await new Promise(requestAnimationFrame);const now=performance.now();samples.push(now-last);last=now;
                const offset=v.camera.position.clone().sub(v.controls.target);offset.applyAxisAngle(v.camera.up,.004);v.camera.position.copy(v.controls.target).add(offset);v.controls.update(); }
              samples.sort((a,b)=>a-b);return {sample_frames:120,median_ms:samples[60],p95_ms:samples[114],mean_fps:1000/(samples.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/samples.length)};
            }''')
            before=page.evaluate('window.blueprintViewer.getSnapshot().camera_position')
            box=canvas.bounding_box()
            page.mouse.move(box['x']+box['width']*.45,box['y']+box['height']*.5)
            page.mouse.down();page.mouse.move(box['x']+box['width']*.65,box['y']+box['height']*.6,steps=12);page.mouse.up()
            page.wait_for_timeout(500)
            assert page.evaluate('window.blueprintViewer.getSnapshot().camera_position')!=before
            page.mouse.wheel(0,-200);page.wait_for_timeout(350)
            page.locator('#fit-model').click()
            page.wait_for_timeout(300)
            assert not interactions
            page.remove_listener('request',listener)
            snap=page.evaluate('window.blueprintViewer.getSnapshot()')
            case['render_info']=snap.get('render_info')
            case['concept_build_count']=snap['concept_build_count']
            assert snap['concept_build_count']==1
            assert page.evaluate('window.originalViewer===window.blueprintViewer && window.initialSceneJSON===JSON.stringify(window.blueprintViewer.data)')
            case['deterministic_interaction_api_calls']=len(interactions)
            case['webgl_renderer']=page.evaluate('''()=>{const gl=window.blueprintViewer.renderer.getContext();const ext=gl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info');return ext?gl.getParameter(ext.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL):gl.getParameter(gl.RENDERER)}''')
            if label=='11397' and args.live_qa:
                health=page.request.get(args.url+'/api/health').json()
                assert health['provider']=='gemini' and health['provider_ready']
                case['live_qa']=[]
                for question,expected in [('What rooms are labeled on the second floor?', 'answered'),('What is the actual ceiling height of this building?', 'insufficient')]:
                    page.locator('#question').fill(question)
                    start=time.perf_counter()
                    with page.expect_response(lambda r:r.url.endswith('/api/ask') and r.request.method=='POST',timeout=180000) as response:
                        page.locator('#ask-button').click()
                    result=response.value.json()
                    case['live_qa'].append({'question':question,'http':response.value.status,'status':result.get('status'),'gate':result.get('gate',{}).get('decision'),'citations':len(result.get('evidence',[])),'highlights':len(result.get('highlight_ids',[])),'seconds':round(time.perf_counter()-start,2)})
                    assert response.value.status==200 and result['status']==expected, case['live_qa'][-1]
                    page.locator('#ask-progress').wait_for(state='hidden')
                page.locator('#result').screenshot(path=str(args.output/'11397-live-height-refusal.png'))
                assert page.evaluate('window.blueprintViewer.getSnapshot().concept_build_count')==1
            page.locator('#show-model').click()
            room=next(e for e in scene['elements'] if e['kind']=='room' and e['geometry'])
            page.locator('#element-select').select_option(room['id'])
            page.locator('#show-assumptions').check()
            page.evaluate('(id)=>window.blueprintViewer.setHighlights([id],true)',room['id'])
            assert any(e['opacity']==.1 for e in page.evaluate('window.blueprintViewer.getSnapshot().elements'))
            page.locator('#element-source').click()
            assert page.locator('#evidence-overlay').is_visible()
            page.locator('#show-comparison').check()
            assert page.locator('#comparison-overlay [data-element-id]').count()>0
            page.locator('#image-stage').screenshot(path=str(args.output/f'{label}-source.png'))
            page.locator('#show-model').click()
            with page.expect_download() as download:page.locator('#download-ifc').click()
            downloaded=args.output/f'{label}-roundtrip.ifc';download.value.save_as(downloaded)
            assert downloaded.read_bytes()==path.read_bytes()
            case['source_overlay_highlight_export_unchanged']=True
            page.locator('#show-concept').click()
            assert page.evaluate('window.blueprintViewer.getSnapshot().concept_build_count')==1
            page.set_viewport_size({'width':390,'height':844})
            assert page.evaluate('document.documentElement.scrollWidth<=innerWidth')
            page.locator('.source-panel').screenshot(path=str(args.output/f'{label}-mobile.png'))
            page.set_viewport_size({'width':1600,'height':1100})
            report['cases'].append(case)
            (args.output/'report.json').write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2))
        report['javascript_errors']=errors
        assert not errors,errors
        (args.output/'report.json').write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2))
        print(json.dumps(report,indent=2))
        browser.close()

if __name__=='__main__':main()
